texts.preamble: Ravindra Singh Tomar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2026 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Gwalior Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice Ashish Shroti Writ Petition No.8280 Of 2023 Ravindra Singh Tomar Versus State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this writ petition challenging the order, dated 27.07.2022, (Annexure P-1) whereby punishment of recovery of Rs.6,26,260/- has been imposed upon the petitioner. This amount also includes Rs.60858/- towards compound interest. The amount was directed to be recovered in monthly instalments of Rs.16,260/-. The petitioner has also challenged the order, dated 19.01.2023, (Annexure P/2) whereby his appeal is partly allowed and the recovery of amount towards interest has been [LEAKAGE_MASK]. The amount of recovery has thus been reduced to Rs.5,65,402/-. He has been also imposed with the punishment of censure. 2. The petitioner, at the relevant time was posted as Beat Guard in Seondha Range, Forest Division, Datia. In relation to certain illegal excavation of the minerals, a charge-sheet under Rule 16 of M.P. Civil Services (Classification, Control & Appeal) Rules, 1966 was issued to the petitioner on 07.04.2021. The petitioner gave detailed reply to this charge-sheet on 18.11.2021 and, thereafter, the respondents have passed the impugned order on 27.07.2022, whereby the petitioner was found guilty of dereliction of duty, as a result of which loss of Rs.5,65,402/- which was caused to the Government, has been directed to be recovered from the petitioner. He was also censured. The appeal filed by his is also decided as stated above. Challenging these orders, the petitioner has filed the present writ petition.
texts.arguments: 3. The learned counsel for the petitioner challenged the impugned order of punishment on two grounds. Firstly, he submitted that since the petitioner raised disputed question of facts in his reply, a detailed departmental enquiry ought to have been conducted by the respondents under Rule 14 of CCA Rules. Counsel for the petitioner placed reliance upon the Apex Court judgment in the case of O.K. Bharadwaj Vs. Union of India & others reported in (2001)9 SCC 180. Secondly, on merits also, Ravindra Singh Tomar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24979716/ 1 no misconduct is committed by the petitioner. The learned counsel for the petitioner thus challenged the finding recorded against the petitioner in the impugned order on merits also. He, therefore, prayed for setting aside the impugned orders. 4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents supported the impugned order and submitted that admittedly at the relevant time, the petitioner was posted as Beat Guard in Seondha Range, Forest Division, Datia, wherein illegal excavation of minerals were found. He further submitted that the petitioner has not disputed the fact that he was responsible for the safety and security of the forest range and, therefore, since the loss is caused to the Government during the period of his posting, he has been rightly imposed with the punishment of recovery of the amount of loss caused to the Government. He further submitted that the respondent Divisional Forest Officer was competent to impose punishment upon the petitioner. He also argued that since recovery of amount is a minor punishment, detailed enquiry as required under Rule 14 of CCA Rules was not conducted. He thus prayed for dismissal of writ petition. Rule 16(1) reads as under:- "1. Subject to the provisions of sub-rule (3) of Rule 15, no order imposing on a Government servant any of the penalties specified in clauses (i) to (iv) of Rule 10 and Rule 11 shall be made except after- (a) informing the Government servant in writing of the proposal to take action against him and of the imputations of misconduct or misbehaviour on which it is proposed to be taken, and giving him a reasonable opportunity of making such representation as he may wish to make against the proposal; (b) holding an inquiry in the manner laid down in sub- rules (3) to (23) of Rule 14, in every case in which the disciplinary authority is of the opinion that such inquiry is necessary; (c) taking the representation, if any, submitted by the Government servant under clause (a) and the record of inquiry, if any, held under clause (b) into consideration; (d) recording a finding on each imputation of misconduct or misbehaviour; and (e) consulting the commission where such consultation is necessary. Ravindra Singh Tomar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24979716/ 2 (1-a) Notwithstanding anything contained in clause (b) of sub-rule (1), if in a case it is proposed after considering the representation, if any, made by the Government Servant under clause (a) of that sub-rule to withhold increments of pay of Stagnation Allowance and such withholding or increments of pay or Stagnation Allowance is likely to effect adversely the amount of pension payable to the Government Servant or to withhold increments of pay or Stagnation allowance for a period exceeding three years of to withhold increments of pay or Stagnation allowance with cumulative effect for any period, an inquiry shall be held in the manner laid down in sub-rules (3) to (23) of Rule 14, before making any order imposing on the Government servant any such penalty." 8. Thus, under clause (b) of Rule 16(1), the disciplinary authority has been given liberty to form an opinion as to whether enquiry as contemplated under Rule 14 is required in the facts and circumstances of the case or not? 9. Pari materia provisions of Regulation 16 of the Food Corporation of India (Staff) Regulations, 1971 were under considered by the Apex Court in the case of the Food Corporation of India, Hyderabad & others Vs. Prahalada Rao & another reported in (2001)1 SCC 165 wherein the Court held in para 5 as under:- "5. Regulation 60(1)(b) mandates the disciplinary authority to form its opinion whether it is necessary to hold inquiry in a particular case or not. Further, Regulation 60(2) itself provides that in a case if it is proposed to withhold increments of pay and such withholding of increments is likely to affect adversely the amount of retirement benefits payable to an employee and in such other cases as mentioned therein, the disciplinary authority shall hold inquiry in the manner laid down in Regulation 58 before making any order imposing any such penalty. It also erred in holding that where an employee denies that loss is caused to the Corporation either by his negligence or breach of order, such inquiry should be held. It is settled law that court's power of judicial review in such cases is limited and court can interfere where the authority held the inquiry proceedings in a manner inconsistent with the rules of natural justice or in violation of statutory rules prescribing the mode of inquiry and imposing punishment or where the conclusion Ravindra Singh Tomar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24979716/ 3 or finding reached by the disciplinary authority is based on no evidence or is such that no reasonable person would have ever reached. As per the Regulation, holding of regular departmental enquiry is a discretionary power of the disciplinary authority which is to be exercised by considering the facts of each case and if it is misused or used arbitrarily, it would be subject to judicial review." 10. Learned counsel for the petitioner relied upon judgment of the Apex Court in the case of O.K. Bhardwaj (supra) to say that full-fledged departmental enquiry ought to have been conducted. The judgments rendered in the case of O.K. Bhardwaj and FCI (supra) have been reconciled by the Division Bench of this Court in the case of Union of India & another Vs. C.P. Singh reported in 2004(2) MPJR 252 (= 2004 SCC Online MP 811). The Court held as under:- "Position after decision in FCI: Where the Rules give a discretion to the Disciplinary Authority to either hold a summary enquiry or regular enquiry, it is not possible to say that the Disciplinary Authority should direct only a regular enquiry, when an employee denies the charge or requests for an inquiry. If he decides not to hold a regular enquiry and proceeds to decide the matter summarily, the employee can always challenge the minor punishment imposed, on the ground that the decision not to hold a regular enquiry was an arbitrary decision.
